messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] Accessing the simulated networks
messages.body_plain:
Dear RSiena experts,
I'm trying to use the simulation engine in RSiena for fixed network models.
That is, the output I'm interested in is the networks in the $sims 
portion of an
RSiena estimation object, not the estimation results itself. My problem is
that I'm only getting "NULL" in the $sims list.
I'm using R 2.12.0 and RSiena 1.0.11.119.

Here's a simple example of what I'm trying to do, and the problem:

library(statnet)  ## to get the random graph function rgraph
two <- rgraph(20,m=2,tprob=0.2)
two[1,,] <- 0  ## set the 1st graph to empty
two[1,sample(1:20,1),sample(1:20,1)]<-1  ## make the 1st graph have only 
1 random tie
two.siena <- sienaNet(array(c(two[1,,],two[2,,]),dim=c(20,20,2)))
two.siena.data <- sienaDataCreate(two.siena)
two.siena.model <- sienaModelCreate(useStdInits = FALSE, projname = 
'two',n3=10)
two.effects <- getEffects(two.siena.data)
two.effects$fix <- two.effects$include ## to fix all the parameters
two.1 <- siena07(two.siena.model,data=two.siena.data,effects=two.effects)
two.1$sims
[[1]]
NULL

[[2]]
NULL

[[3]]
NULL

[[4]]
NULL

[[5]]
NULL

The errors from the siena07 process are:
> Error in solve.default(z$msfc) :
>   Lapack routine dgesv: system is exactly singular
> In addition: Warning message:
> In max(abs(tstat)[!z$fixed & !z$BasicRateFunction & z$resist > 0.9]) :
>   no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf

I'm attaching the out file from this process.

Any ideas as to what I'm doing wrong?
Thanks so much!
Best,
Brian



-- 
Brian Rubineau
Assistant Professor, Organizational Behavior        394 Ives Hall
School of Industrial and Labor Relations         ph. 607.255.3048
Cornell University                              fax. 607.255.2261
Ithaca, NY 14853                            brubineau at cornell.edu

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] New Memory Issue
messages.body_plain:
Hi group.

I have a very large time series. I am analyzing it by dividing it into small
sections. I estimate parameters for many small sections of time and combine
them using siena08(). I have done this using 54 individual estimations in
the past with little trouble on a machine with 4 gigabytes of RAM.

Recently, I have tried this again with no success. R spits out a memory
error, even if I use a machine with 8 gigabytes of memory and the 64bit
version of R and the OS. The problem is that all of the sienaFit objects
need to be loaded and there has to be enough memory left for siena08() to do
its job. I have tried breaking the estimations down into theoretically
interesting subsets, but that still results in a set of sienaFit objects of
size 40--still too big. Also, if I monitor the computer's RAM usage, it
clearly sky rockets when I load() the saved sienaFit objects. In fact, the
sienaFit objects appear to consume more memory than they have in the past.

I am currently using RSiena version 141. First, I want to confirm that
RSiena is actually storing more information in the sienaFit objects in
recent updates of the software. Second, if this is true, and short of
finding a machine with more RAM, does anyone have a suggestion for working
around the resulting problem? Thank you.

Nathan Doogan
Doctoral Student
The Ohio State University

each version.

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] Accessing the simulated networks
messages.body_plain:
Dear Brian,

You need to ask for the simulations to be returned. Use returnDeps=TRUE in 
the call to siena07.

By the way, you can turn off estimation by using nsub=0 in the call to 
sienaModelCreate. If you do this, you do not need to fix the parameters.

Regards,

Ruth

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] undirected networks in RSiena
messages.body_plain:
greetings,

i wonder if anyone can provide an update on current functionality for 
undirected networks in RSiena? it appears that RSiena indeed recognizes 
my network as undirected, but this case is not as thoroughly documented 
in the most recent manual. in particular i am wondering about the following:

1) if i recall correctly, version 3 did not allow estimation by the 
score function method, and instead forced the "finite differences" 
method for all undirected models. however, when i run an undirected 
model in RSiena, it seems i am able to select the score function method 
without problem (and the output reports that standard errors are 
estimated with the likelihood ratio method, which i assume is the same 
thing). am i correct in interpreting this to mean that the score 
function method is now available for undirected networks in RSiena?

2) while RSiena will successfully run an undirected model, the "model 
options" screen still looks identical to the options screen for directed 
networks- and therefore i am unable to select which of the 6 undirected 
model types i would like to use (a possibility that was available in 
version 3). the output reports, however, that "Model Type 2: Forcing 
model" appears to be the default. is there a way to change this to 
another type, in particular the initiative-confirmation model? if not, 
is there reason to believe this will influence results anyway? (i recall 
reading somewhere that results did not vary much across different 
undirected model types.)

i am obviously also using the GUI, so perhaps this is something i can 
accomplish without the GUI.

thanks for any help with this!

-kevin

-- 
Kevin Lewis
Ph.D. Candidate in Sociology
Harvard University
33 Kirkland Street
Cambridge, MA 02138

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] undirected networks in RSiena
messages.body_plain:
Kevin,

1) There is an option called modelType which is not available via the GUI.
The documentation is rudimentary at the moment, I am afraid. 
?sienaModelCreate will tell you the possible values. I think 3 is what you 
need.

2) It is no longer necessary to use the finite difference method for 
undirected networks.

Hope this helps,

Ruth
